intro: What you have in stock, in each place, and every way it changes: transfers between places, counts, corrections and moves between inventory types. A quantity is never typed over; each change is a movement with the document that caused it.
start: Open Stock levels and choose a place, to see what it holds and at what price.
Set reorder levels for the items you must not run out of.
Count your stock once, so the books start from what is really on the shelf.
Check Inventory types under Setup, so you know which kinds of stock can be sold.

articles.title: See how much stock you have
articles.summary: Stock levels shows what each place holds, what is running low and every movement behind the figures.

steps.rest: and choose the place.
by name or SKU. Each row shows what is on hand, the reorder level and the price there.

tips: Stock held for production is set aside for a work order and is not for sale. It shows as a line of its own.
Stock on its way between places is counted but not available at either end.

articles.title: Get told when to buy more, and order it
articles.summary: Set the levels for each item at each place, then let Clafina draft the requisitions for whatever has fallen below them.

steps.rest: Stock records are listed against their levels, worst first.

steps.lead: Tick the items and press Set levels….
steps.rest: Enter the minimum, safety level, reorder point and reorder quantity, each at least as high as the one before.
Each row now shows where it stands: out of stock, below the minimum, below the safety level, at the reorder point, or fine.
You see what would be ordered for each place and about what it costs, before anything is made.
A draft purchase requisition is made for each place. Nothing goes to a supplier: a buyer reviews it and sends it on.

tips: Stock already on its way to a place is counted before an order is suggested.
A level is set per item per place.

articles.title: Move stock from one place to another
articles.summary: Draw up a transfer, send it, and receive it at the other end. While it travels it is counted, but cannot be sold.

Where your settings ask for approval, the button reads Save and send for approval, and it waits. Once approved, press Send it.

steps.lead: At the other end, press Receive.
steps.rest: Say who counted it and how much of each item arrived.

steps.lead: Say what happens to anything missing:
steps.rest: leave it on the road for now, or write it off as lost in transit.

tips: On the road, by item lists everything travelling between places, and which transfers are late.
A transfer that has not left can be called off.

articles.title: Count your stock and correct the books
articles.summary: Count what is on the shelf; when you approve the count, the differences are posted with the reason you gave.

steps.rest: on Stock counts.

Approval uses what is saved.
A correction is posted for each line that differs, to make stock match what you counted. It cannot be undone.

tips: With blind counts on in Settings, what is expected of a line shows only once you have saved your count of it.
A line nobody counted is not taken as zero.

articles.title: Correct a quantity by hand
articles.summary: Say what the quantity is, or how much to add or take away, with a reason. Where your settings ask, it waits for approval first.

steps.lead: On Stock levels, choose Adjust quantity
steps.rest: on the item's row.

The drawer shows what the system holds and what it will hold after.

The quantities change only when its approvers agree.

tips: Whether a correction needs a request, and above what value, is set in Settings › Stock and prices.
Where quantities change only through documents, use a goods receipt, a transfer or a count instead.

articles.title: Move stock to another inventory type
articles.summary: Move goods at one place from one type to another, such as from awaiting release to sellable, for a reason you choose. Their value does not change.

steps.rest: on Type transfers.

tips: Settings › Type transfers say which types stock may leave and arrive in, and the reasons you can choose.
A type transfer that has moved stock can be reversed.

articles.summary: Stock classes rank items by the value that leaves stock, and say which are due for a count.
